title: Design system v0 - tokens, primitives, Storybook
body:
## Context
CandleViewer is a dense, dark-first, desktop-only professional trading terminal. Every R1+ screen (`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`) must be assembled from tokens and shared primitives rather than bespoke CSS, otherwise the 238 catalogued components (`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md#8-summary-tallies`) drift into 238 one-off styles and WCAG 2.2 AA conformance (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`) becomes unverifiable. E05 delivers **design system v0**: the three-tier token model, the Style Dictionary build with its six output targets, the three themes (dark / light / high-contrast), the two density modes, the R0/R1-critical atoms and molecules, Storybook with the a11y addon in CI, and a visual-regression baseline.

E05 is design-led and runs the full R0 window S01-S04 (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#42-scope-epics`). It gates E10 (App shell & Electron wrapper) in the epic dependency graph (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#111-epic-dependency-graph`: `E05 --> E10`) and is itself gated by E02 (monorepo scaffold, `packages/ui`) and E03 (CI jobs hosting the a11y / visual-regression / contrast gates).

Product framing comes from the SET story domain (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md#27-set--settings-hotkeys-themes`): US-SET-004 (themes and density), US-SET-005 (colour conventions / CVD-safe palettes) and US-SET-007 (accessibility preferences) are the Must stories whose *system-level* foundations live here. Their settings screens (SCR-116 Appearance & density, SCR-117 Accessibility) are built by the later settings epic; the tokens, theme engine, density engine, reduced-motion primitives and preview primitives those screens consume are E05 deliverables.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Tokens**: `packages/ui/tokens/*.tokens.json` - Tier-1 primitive, Tier-2 semantic, Tier-3 component tokens per `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#2-token-architecture`; colour, typography, spacing, radii, elevation, motion.
- **Token build**: Style Dictionary config with the six binding output targets (`build/css/tokens.{dark,light,high-contrast}.css`, `build/ts/tokens.ts`, `build/engine/theme-uniforms.json`, `build/electron/tokens.main.json`, `build/reports/contrast-matrix.{json,md}`) per `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#11-handoff-spec-tokens-json--code`.
- **Theme + density runtime**: `ThemeProvider`, `data-theme` / `data-density` root attributes, instant no-reload swap, `prefers-reduced-motion` + explicit in-app override, theme-change event consumed later by the WebGL engine.
- **Components** (R0/R1-critical subset of `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md`): atoms CMP-001..CMP-039, molecules CMP-040..CMP-050, CMP-054, CMP-059, CMP-062, CMP-063, CMP-065, CMP-069, plus CMP-079 RbacGate, CMP-085 SkipLink, CMP-089 ForbiddenState, CMP-090 NotFoundState, CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback, CMP-228 PreviewTile.
- **Storybook 8** with `@storybook/addon-a11y`, theme + density toolbar switchers, test-runner in CI (`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`).
- **Visual-regression baseline** across variant x theme(3) x density(2).
- **Contrast-matrix CI gate** (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text/chart ink, 7:1 `.hc` buy/sell).
- **Icon registry** incl. trading-domain custom icons (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#5-iconography`).
- **ADR-0016** design-token architecture & theming.
- Design tickets (UX research, Figma Foundations + component library, motion spec, a11y/CVD sign-off, design QA, handoff), QA tickets (component test plan, a11y audit, VR regression pack + sign-off), security tickets (STRIDE, security review).

## Out of scope
- Android / mobile / responsive breakpoints below 1280x800 (locked out, `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`).
- Settings screens SCR-110..SCR-119 themselves (later settings epic) - E05 ships only the primitives they consume.
- Trading-specific components CMP-100..CMP-139, rule-engine CMP-140..CMP-159, watchlist/journal CMP-160..CMP-179, chart primitives CMP-180..CMP-199 (E11+ epics).
- App shell organisms CMP-070..CMP-084 and CMP-086/CMP-087 layouts (E10) - E05 supplies their tokens and atoms only.
- Final brand skin: the system is brand-neutral; colour/logo swap is a later token-only change.
- Options/GEX, mobile, separate admin app - out of product scope entirely.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Design system v0 published
  Given R0 exit criterion 8 (docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#43-exit-criteria)
  When Storybook is built from main
  Then tokens are published, at least 25 components have stories, axe-core reports zero serious/critical violations
  And dark, light and high-contrast themes are each selectable and rendered
Scenario: Instant theme swap
  Given any Storybook story or app surface is open
  When the theme is switched
  Then every surface updates within one frame with no reload and no component remount
Scenario: Contrast gate blocks a bad token
  Given a PR lowers color.text.secondary lightness below 4.5:1 on surface.app
  When CI runs the contrast-matrix check
  Then the build fails and names the offending token pair
Scenario: No hardcoded values
  When the lint rule forbidding raw hex/px in packages/ui runs
  Then it reports zero violations outside tokens/ source files
Scenario: Density is spacing-only
  Given any catalogued component story
  When density switches from compact to comfortable
  Then the DOM structure is identical and only spacing/row-height values differ
```

## Technical notes / design
- Package: `packages/ui` (pnpm workspace, created by E02). Public entry exports components plus generated `tokens.ts` typings; no app state, no `fetch`, no Bybit knowledge (CONSTITUTION module-edge rules enforced by `import-linter`/ESLint boundaries).
- Token naming `category.subcategory.variant.state` maps 1:1 to `--color-text-buy` CSS custom properties and to Figma Variables names, so design/code diffs are mechanical.
- Themes are token re-pointing, never new token names. Light is separately tuned, not an inversion.
- Density selects which spacing scale steps the component aliases resolve to; component structure never branches on density.
- Custom Style Dictionary formats `json/flat-rgba` and `json/flat` live in `tools/style-dictionary/formats/`.

## Test plan
Rolled up from children: Vitest unit tests per component (props/variants/states), Storybook interaction tests (play functions) via the Storybook test runner, `vitest-axe` per story, visual-regression snapshots per variant x theme x density, contrast-matrix script unit tests, and a Playwright smoke that switches theme/density on the Storybook docs page. Coverage target >=80% lines on `packages/ui` (frontend threshold, `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`).

## Security notes
Low intrinsic risk (no secrets, no PII, no money movement, data classification: public/internal). Real threats are **supply chain** (Storybook, Style Dictionary, icon library dependency tree - typosquat/compromised package executing at build time), **published Storybook exposure** (must remain Tailscale-only per `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md`), and **CSP regressions** from inline-style token injection. Covered by E05-X01 (STRIDE) and E05-X02 (review). Security label required at epic level.

## Accessibility notes
E05 is the epic that makes WCAG 2.2 AA achievable downstream: focus-ring token >=3:1 against every surface tier, 24x24px compact minimum target with documented essential-exceptions, colour-never-alone enforcement, motion-safe/motion-reduce pairs, and CVD-safe buy/sell pairs (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 4, 5, 7, 11). Gate: axe-core zero serious/critical across all stories plus Accessibility-role sign-off (`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#13-design-ahead-process--sign-off-definition`).

## Performance notes
Theme/density switch must complete within one frame (<=16.6 ms) and must never remount panels or drop a WebGL context (SCR-116 Performance, `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`). Token CSS bundle <=40 KB gzipped per theme. Storybook CI job <=10 min so the R0 "commit to dev deploy <=15 min" pipeline budget holds.

## Observability
Analytics events defined here and emitted by downstream settings screens: `appearance.theme_changed`, `appearance.density_changed`, `appearance.font_size_changed`, `appearance.chart_palette_changed`, `a11y.preference_changed`. CI publishes the contrast-matrix report and VR diff artifacts per PR.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All child tickets Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] R0 exit criterion 8 demonstrably met (Storybook published, >=25 components, zero axe violations, 3 themes).
- [ ] Coverage >=80% on `packages/ui`; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] ADR-0016 merged; `16-design-system-brief.md` and `15-component-catalogue.md` updated to shipped reality.
- [ ] CDO design sign-off recorded (R0 quality gate "Design", `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#44-quality-gates`).
- [ ] Accessibility-role sign-off recorded; manual screen-reader pass on the exemplar stories.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment present; SCA/secrets scan clean.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded.
- [ ] Demoed to the Owner at a Sprint Review.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E02` - `packages/ui` workspace, toolchain, lint/test runners (`E02 --> E05`).
- `blocked_by: E03` - CI jobs that host the Storybook/a11y/VR/contrast gates.
- Blocks `E10` (app shell & Electron wrapper) and transitively every R1 screen epic.

## Branch
`feat/design-system-<short>` per child ticket; PRs <=400 LOC; the `tokens/` directory is versioned independently with its own CHANGELOG.

## Risks

- **R2 Render performance**: a theme swap that remounts panels would drop GL contexts mid-session; explicitly tested in T02.
- **Design-ahead slip**: if D01/D02 slip past S02, S01..S04 cannot start Ready. Tracked as the epic's top schedule risk.

## Design-ahead waiver (Architect + CDO, recorded 2026-09-14)
E05 is the *design-system epic itself*: its "design" tickets (E05-D01/D02/D03/D06) and its "engineering" tickets are produced by the same co-located design-system pod inside a single 4-sprint R0 window (S01-S04, `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md#42-scope-epics`), so the normal ">=2 sprints Done-before-consumption" gap of `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (Team & cadence) and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1 cannot be satisfied without pushing E05 past the R0 train and blocking E10 and every R1 screen epic.

**Waiver scope (explicit, time-boxed, R0-only):** the 1-sprint gap on the following intra-epic design->code edges only:
- E05-D01 (Done S01) -> E05-T01 (S02)
- E05-D02 (Done S02) -> E05-S01 (S03), E05-T06 (S03)
- E05-D03 (Done S02) -> E05-T02 (S03)
- E05-D06 (Done S02) -> E05-S01 (S03)

**Granted by:** Architect and Chief Design Officer. **Reason:** foundational bootstrap epic; design and implementation share one pod and one Figma/token source of truth; no external design consumer exists in R0.
**Compensating controls:** (a) design-token handoff is mechanical (Figma Variables names == token names, E05-D06), so late design churn is a token-value diff, not a component rewrite; (b) E05-D05 design QA and E05-D04 a11y/CVD sign-off run in S04 before the epic closes; (c) any component whose Figma spec is not Done at the start of its implementation sprint is descoped from v0 rather than implemented speculatively; (d) E05-S02/S03/S04 (S04) already satisfy the full >=2-sprint rule against E05-D02.
**Expiry:** this waiver does NOT extend past R0. All R1+ screen epics consume E05 design output with the full >=2-sprint gap (E05 design artefacts are Done by S02/S04, R1 starts S05).

## Estimate reconciliation (roadmap vs backlog)
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` lines 105 and 188 carried **34 pts** for E05. The decomposed backlog totals **38 engineering points** (Story+Task+Spike, excluding design/QA/security discipline tickets) and **78 points all-in** across all 24 children. The 34 figure was a pre-decomposition T-shirt estimate that omitted E05-T06 (icon registry, 2) and under-counted the molecule band (E05-S03, 5 vs 3). The roadmap has been updated to **38 pts** to match this backlog; the backlog is the source of truth and the epic `estimate` field (78) is the all-in rollup of every child. Breakdown:
- Engineering (Story/Task/Spike): 38 = S01 8 + S02 5 + S03 5 + S04 3 + T01 5 + T02 3 + T03 2 + T04 2 + T05 1 + T06 2 + T07 1 + K01 1 (design-discipline Tasks D01/D02/D03/D06/D07 excluded).
- Design discipline (D01-D07): 27. QA (Q01-Q03): 9. Security (X01-X02): 4.
- All-in rollup: 78 (epic `estimate`). R0 capacity impact is unchanged: 38 engineering pts spread over S01-S04 against a ~90 pts/sprint team velocity.


## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently: backend (`api`/`data-feeds`) tickets, frontend (`web`) tickets and design (`-D*`) tickets form separate lanes once their own upstream design/contract tickets are Done. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: UX research: density, numeric legibility and CVD palette validation
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#1-design-principles` locks 'legibility of numbers over decoration' and 'density is a mode, not a compromise', and `#3-density-modes` proposes compact 24px / comfortable 36px row heights. Those numbers, the mono numeric family choice, and the two colour-blind-safe buy/sell pairs required by `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#4-colour-independence-for-buysell-and-all-status-signalling` are currently **proposals, not validated findings**. Because every downstream component (CMP-001..CMP-238) resolves its spacing and colour from these decisions, validating them once here is far cheaper than re-tuning 238 components later. US-SET-004 (themes and density, Must) and US-SET-005 (colour conventions / CVD-safe palettes, Must) depend on the outcome.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Moderated sessions with the Owner and the account-manager personas (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`) on scanning speed for a positions grid and a DOM ladder at compact vs comfortable row heights.
- Numeric legibility test: candidate `font.family.mono` faces (tabular-figure UI variant vs dedicated mono) at `font.size.xs`/`sm` on `surface.app` and `surface.canvas`.
- CVD validation: simulate deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia over the two candidate `color.buy`/`color.sell` pairs plus the two heatmap ramps (`heatmap.convention.green-bid-red-ask`, `heatmap.convention.red-bid-green-ask`).
- Confirm or revise: compact row height, compact field height, the 24x24px minimum-target essential-exception list, default density per surface class.
- Output: research report in `docs/research/` plus a decisions block appended to `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#3-density-modes`, feeding E05-D01 and E05-T01.

## Out of scope
- No Figma component production (that is E05-D01/E05-D02).
- No code.
- No mobile/responsive research (desktop-only, locked).
- No brand/visual-identity exploration.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Density decision is evidence-backed
  Given at least 3 participant sessions covering positions-grid and DOM-ladder scanning
  When the report is published
  Then compact and comfortable row/field heights are stated as final values with the measured rationale
  And any deviation from the brief's 24px/36px proposal is recorded as a brief amendment
Scenario: CVD pairs validated
  Given the candidate buy/sell pairs and both heatmap ramps
  When each is run through deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia simulation
  Then exactly two buy/sell pairs are recommended as CVD-safe with simulation screenshots attached
  And any ramp stop that becomes indistinguishable from its neighbour under simulation is flagged for re-tuning
Scenario: Essential-exception list produced
  Given compact-mode controls that cannot reach 24x24px without breaking information density
  When the report is published
  Then each such control is listed by CMP-* id with its compensating control (click-tolerance padding, adjacent spacing)
  And any control not on this list must meet 24x24px unconditionally
Scenario: Mono face is decided
  When legibility results are compared
  Then one font.family.mono candidate is selected, or the decision is explicitly deferred with the blocking question named
```

## Technical notes / design
Method: moderated task-based sessions (find-the-largest-loss, find-the-price-level) timed and error-counted; the stimulus is a static high-fidelity mock, not a build. CVD simulation via a Figma plugin plus an offline pass using a CIELAB-based simulation script so results are reproducible in CI later. Heatmap ramps are evaluated in OKLCH/CIELAB interpolation as required by `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#6-data-viz-rules` rule 2 - naive RGB lerp is explicitly rejected and must not be used to produce the stimuli.

## Test plan
N/A for automated tests. Verification is peer review of the report by the Accessibility role and the CDO; the CVD simulation script is handed to E05-T05 as the seed for the automated contrast/CVD check.

## Security notes
No secrets, no PII beyond participant first names - store session notes without identifying details. Data classification: internal. No security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket is itself an accessibility input: its CVD findings are a binding input to `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#42` conformance and to the contrast-matrix thresholds. At least one participant session should include a participant using increased OS text scale to sanity-check the 125%/200% zoom reflow assumption.

## Performance notes
N/A - no runtime component. Density findings indirectly affect the number of rendered rows per viewport and therefore the R1 grid performance budget in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

## Observability
N/A.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Report published under `docs/research/` and linked from this ticket.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md` sections 3 and 2.1 amended with final values (or explicitly confirmed unchanged).
- [ ] CVD simulation artefacts attached.
- [ ] Essential-exception list produced and accepted by the Accessibility role.
- [ ] Findings presented at Design Review; E05-D01 moved to Ready.
- [ ] CDO acknowledgement recorded.

## Dependencies
No blockers - deliberately first so the design-ahead chain has a validated starting point. Blocks E05-D01 (Figma Foundations) because token values depend on these findings.

## Branch
`design/design-system-ux-research` (docs/report only); PR small, docs-only.

- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md sections 4, 5

title: Specify motion recipes with motion-safe/motion-reduce pairs
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#7-motion` defines purposeful-motion-only rules and six standard recipes, each requiring an explicit `motion-safe`/`motion-reduce` pair; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#7-reduced-motion` makes the reduce pair binding and forbids any information being carried by motion alone. US-SET-007 (Accessibility preferences, Must) requires reduced motion to disable heatmap fades, panel transitions and chart inertia. Engineering (E05-T02) needs a precise, per-property spec rather than the prose in the brief.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A motion spec table: for each recipe (panel focus/mount, dialog/drawer open, value flash on price tick, toast enter/exit, node-graph edge draw, loading shimmer) give the animated CSS property, the `motion.duration.*` and `motion.easing.*` tokens, and the exact `motion-reduce` substitute.
- Rules encoded as checkable statements: no flashing above 3 Hz; no looping motion beyond 5 s without a pause control; motion is never the sole carrier of information.
- Prototype frames in Figma demonstrating each recipe in safe and reduce variants.
- The value-flash recipe specified for both themes, since a background flash that reads as 'up' in dark must not read as 'down' in light.
- Spec for the in-app Reduce Motion override (Settings -> Appearance) layering over the OS `prefers-reduced-motion` signal, including precedence: explicit in-app choice wins over OS.

## Out of scope
- Chart-engine internal animation (inertia, heatmap trail decay) beyond stating the reduce-mode requirement; engine implementation is E11.
- Implementation code (E05-T02).
- Marketing/brand motion.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every recipe has a reduce pair
  Given the motion spec table
  When any recipe row is read
  Then it names an explicit motion-reduce substitute, and 'none' is written literally rather than left blank
Scenario: No information lost under reduce
  Given the value-flash recipe
  When reduce mode is active
  Then the price direction is still conveyed by a colour tint and a glyph, not by the absent flash
Scenario: Flash-rate safety
  Given a fast-ticking price under maximum update rate
  Then the specified flash cannot exceed 3 occurrences per second; the spec states the coalescing rule that enforces it
Scenario: Override precedence
  Given the OS reports prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and the user enables in-app Reduce Motion
  Then the spec requires reduced motion to apply
```

## Technical notes / design
Durations: `instant` 0 ms, `fast` 100 ms, `normal` 200 ms, `slow` 400 ms. Reduce substitutes: transition removed (instant state change) or a non-motion cue (opacity-only pulse instead of scale+rotate spinner; static two-tone fill instead of shimmer). Flash coalescing: at most one flash per 333 ms per element, subsequent ticks update the value without re-triggering the animation - this is the mechanism that keeps a fast tape under the 3 Hz ceiling.

## Test plan
Verification by the Accessibility role against `05-accessibility-standard.md#7`. Engineering-side automated checks are specified here and implemented in E05-T02: a unit test asserting every animated property has a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` counterpart, and a story-level test asserting no animation runs when the reduce flag is set.

## Security notes

title: Implement token source of truth and Style Dictionary multi-target build
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#11-handoff-spec-tokens-json--code` specifies the binding build contract: one `style-dictionary build` run produces six artefacts consumed by four distinct consumers (React app, Storybook, the WebGL chart engine, and the Electron main process). Without this build, every consumer would re-declare colours - and the WebGL engine in particular cannot read CSS custom properties inside a GL context, which is precisely why `build/engine/theme-uniforms.json` exists. This task is the single most load-bearing technical deliverable of E05.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/ui/tokens/*.tokens.json` - the authored source, exported from the Figma Foundations file (E05-D01): colour (3 themes), typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, density aliases.
- `style-dictionary.config.json` with the four platforms `css`, `ts`, `engine`, `electron` exactly as sketched in the brief.
- Custom formats `json/flat-rgba` and `json/flat` registered in `tools/style-dictionary/formats/`, with their own unit tests and a README next to the config.
- Outputs: `build/css/tokens.dark.css` (`[data-theme="dark"]`), `build/css/tokens.light.css`, `build/css/tokens.high-contrast.css`, `build/ts/tokens.ts` (typed ES6 declarations), `build/engine/theme-uniforms.json`, `build/electron/tokens.main.json`.
- npm script `pnpm --filter ui tokens:build`, wired into the package build so a stale build cannot be published.
- `tokens/CHANGELOG.md` and independent semver for the token directory.
- ESLint rule forbidding raw hex colours and raw px values in `packages/ui/src/**` (tokens source exempt).

## Out of scope
- The contrast report generation and CI gate (E05-T05, consumes this build).
- Runtime theme switching (E05-T02).
- Consuming the engine uniforms inside the WebGL renderer (E11).
- Figma authoring (E05-D01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: One build, six artefacts
  Given a clean checkout
  When pnpm --filter ui tokens:build runs
  Then all six documented artefact paths exist and are non-empty
  And a second run produces byte-identical output (deterministic build)
Scenario: Theme parity
  Given the three generated CSS files
  When their custom-property name sets are compared
  Then the sets are identical; a token present in one theme and missing in another fails the build with the token name in the error
Scenario: Engine uniforms are numeric RGBA
  Given build/engine/theme-uniforms.json
  Then every chart-category token is emitted as a 4-float RGBA array in 0..1 range, with no CSS syntax and no hex strings
Scenario: Electron main JSON is flat
  Given build/electron/tokens.main.json
  Then it is a single-level key to value map parseable without any CSS or TypeScript tooling
Scenario: Hardcoded value is rejected
  Given a component committing color: #2B6CE8
  When lint runs
  Then it fails naming the file, line and the token that should have been used
Scenario: Stale build cannot ship
  Given tokens/*.tokens.json changed without re-running the build
  When CI runs
  Then the build output diff check fails
```

## Technical notes / design
Token name `category.subcategory.variant.state` -> CSS `--color-text-buy` via the standard `css` transform group; -> TS as a nested typed object so `tokens.color.text.buy` type-checks. The `engine` platform filters `category == "chart"` and converts hex/oklch to linear-ish RGBA floats; document whether values are sRGB 0..1 (chosen: sRGB 0..1, conversion to linear happens in the shader) so E11 does not guess. Theme filtering uses a `theme` attribute on each token. Determinism: sort keys, pin Style Dictionary version, no timestamps in output headers. Error codes: build fails with `TOKENS-E001` missing-theme-parity, `TOKENS-E002` unresolved alias reference, `TOKENS-E003` unknown category for the engine filter.

## Test plan
Unit (Vitest): custom format `json/flat-rgba` converts `#2B6CE8` to the expected RGBA floats; `json/flat` flattens nested input; theme-parity checker detects an intentionally removed token; alias resolver detects a dangling reference. Integration: run the real build in CI and assert all six artefacts exist, are non-empty and are byte-stable across two runs. Contract: a snapshot test of the generated `tokens.ts` public shape so an accidental rename is caught by consumers' CI. Coverage target >=85% on `tools/style-dictionary/` (build tooling treated as engine-grade).

## Security notes
Supply chain: pin Style Dictionary and its transitive deps with a lockfile; the build executes third-party code, so it runs in CI without repository write credentials. No secret may appear in a token file - add a gitleaks path rule over `packages/ui/tokens/`. Data classification: internal, non-sensitive.

## Accessibility notes
This build is the vehicle for a11y enforcement: the contrast report (E05-T05) is generated from these artefacts. Ensure `.hc` variants of buy/sell and the focus-ring token are emitted in all themes so the high-contrast theme is complete rather than partially inheriting dark.

## Performance notes
Each generated theme CSS must be <=40 KB gzipped (epic budget). The build must complete in <=10 s locally so it can run on every `pnpm dev` start without friction.

## Observability
Build emits a one-line summary (token count per category, per theme, output byte sizes) to CI logs so an unexpected token explosion is visible in PR review.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All six artefacts generated and committed-or-ignored per the agreed strategy, documented in `packages/ui/README.md`.
- [ ] Unit + integration tests green; coverage threshold met.
- [ ] ESLint no-raw-value rule enabled and clean.
- [ ] `16-design-system-brief.md#11` updated if the implemented config diverges from the sketch.
- [ ] `tokens/CHANGELOG.md` initialised at 0.1.0.
- [ ] PR merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. code-owner.
- [ ] Before/after evidence shown at Sprint Review (observable-effect Task).

## Dependencies
`blocked_by: E05-D01` (authored Figma variables are the source), `blocked_by: E02` (pnpm workspace and `packages/ui` must exist). Blocks E05-T02, E05-T03, E05-T05, E05-T07 and all component stories.

## Branch
`feat/design-system-tokens`; PR ~350 LOC incl. generated-artefact policy.

## References
- docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md sections 2, 11
- docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md section 5
- docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md (theme-uniform consumer)
- docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md

### Design-ahead waiver
This ticket starts 1 sprint after its design dependency is Done, not the >=2 sprints required by `docs/plan/00-planning-brief.md` (Team & cadence) and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1. title: Implement theme, density and reduced-motion runtime in packages/ui
body:
## Context
US-SET-004 (Must) requires that switching theme updates every surface **including WebGL canvases** immediately without reload; US-SET-007 (Must) requires reduced motion to apply immediately across all views. SCR-116's performance note is binding: theme and density changes are CSS custom-property swaps applied within one frame that never remount panels or drop GL contexts - a naive React re-render at the provider root would violate this and cost a WebGL context restore mid-session (R2). This task builds the runtime that makes that guarantee real.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `ThemeProvider` in `packages/ui/src/theme/`: sets `data-theme` (`dark` | `light` | `high-contrast`) and `data-density` (`compact` | `comfortable`) on `document.documentElement`, never on a React-owned subtree wrapper.
- `useTheme()` / `useDensity()` hooks returning current value and setter; values persisted per user (localStorage in v0, server-backed preference later by the settings epic).
- Optional 'match system' mode for theme, **off by default** (a trading terminal must not flip mid-session).
- `prefers-reduced-motion` detection plus an explicit in-app override, precedence: in-app override wins; exposed as `data-motion="reduce"` root attribute and a `useReducedMotion()` hook.
- A theme-change event (`candleviewer:themechange` CustomEvent with the resolved theme name and the `theme-uniforms` payload key) that the WebGL chart engine subscribes to in E11 - the binding requirement recorded in `docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#4`.
- `Ctrl+Shift+H` high-contrast toggle registered as a design-system-level shortcut contract (the global hotkey registry itself is E10/US-SET-002).
- Motion recipes from E05-D03 implemented as CSS custom properties plus a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block and a `[data-motion="reduce"]` block.
- Font-size scale support (100/112/125/150%) as a root `data-text-scale` attribute so SCR-116 can drive it later.

## Out of scope
- SCR-116 / SCR-117 settings screens themselves (later settings epic).
- The WebGL engine's uniform re-upload (E11) - E05 only emits the event and the payload.
- Server-side persistence of preferences.
- The global hotkey registry (E10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Instant swap without remount
  Given a mounted component tree with an instrumented mount counter
  When the theme is switched from dark to high-contrast
  Then the root data-theme attribute changes, styles update, and the mount counter is unchanged
Scenario: One-frame budget
  Given a story rendering 500 dense table rows
  When theme or density is switched
  Then the style recalculation completes within 16.6 ms measured via the Performance API
Scenario: Engine notification
  Given a listener registered for candleviewer:themechange
  When the theme changes
  Then the listener receives the resolved theme name exactly once per change
Scenario: Reduced motion override beats the OS
  Given the OS reports prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference
  When the in-app Reduce Motion override is enabled
  Then data-motion="reduce" is set and no transition runs on any animated property
Scenario: Density is spacing-only
  Given any component rendered in compact mode
  When density switches to comfortable
  Then the serialized DOM structure is identical and only computed spacing values differ
Scenario: Persisted preference survives reload
  Given a user selected light + comfortable
  When the app reloads
  Then those values are restored before first paint with no flash of the wrong theme
```

## Technical notes / design
No flash-of-wrong-theme: a tiny synchronous inline script in the document head reads the persisted value and sets the root attributes before the first paint - documented as a required snippet that E10's shell must include. Theme switch must not re-render React: the provider stores the theme in a ref-backed external store and only components explicitly subscribing to the value (e.g. CMP-062 ThemeSwitcher's own checked state) re-render. Density likewise. Motion reduce is implemented purely with CSS so the frame budget benefit is real. Event payload: `{ theme: "dark"|"light"|"high-contrast", density: "compact"|"comfortable", motion: "safe"|"reduce" }`.

## Test plan
Unit (Vitest + Testing Library): attribute setting per theme; persistence round-trip; match-system mode off by default; reduced-motion precedence matrix (OS x override = 4 cases); density attribute change does not alter `container.innerHTML` structure. Interaction: Storybook play function toggling theme and asserting no remount via a mount-count decorator. Perf: a benchmark story measuring style-recalc time on a 500-row table across a theme switch, asserted under 16.6 ms. Contract: an assertion that every animated CSS property declared in `packages/ui` has a reduce counterpart (static scan over the compiled CSS). Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
The inline pre-paint script is the only inline script in the app - it must be allowlisted in the Electron CSP by hash, not by `unsafe-inline`, and this requirement is handed to E10 explicitly. Flagged to E05-X01's STRIDE model as a CSP-weakening temptation.

## Accessibility notes
Directly implements US-SET-007 reduced motion and the high-contrast theme required by `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#56`. `Ctrl+Shift+H` must be announced to screen readers via a polite live region when it toggles. Text-scale support must reflow rather than clip at 125% and 200% zoom.

## Performance notes
Hard budget: <=16.6 ms style recalculation on the 500-row benchmark; zero component remounts; zero WebGL context loss. Reduce mode must measurably lower per-frame transition work (recorded as a before/after number).

## Observability
Emit `appearance.theme_changed`, `appearance.density_changed` and `a11y.preference_changed` via an injectable analytics callback (no-op by default in `packages/ui`, wired by the app) so the package stays framework/app-agnostic.

## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#11` requires `build/reports/contrast-matrix.json` plus a human-readable `.md`, generated in the same build step, with CI failing a token PR if any required pair drops below its threshold (4.5:1 text, 3:1 non-text/chart ink, 7:1 buy/sell high-contrast). `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md#54` additionally requires every heatmap ramp stop to be independently validated against the chart background. ## Scope / Deliverables
- `tools/contrast/` script consuming the generated token artefacts from E05-T01.

- Outputs `build/reports/contrast-matrix.json` and `.md`.
- CVD simulation check (deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia) asserting adjacent heatmap ramp stops and the buy/sell pair remain distinguishable, using the simulation method fixed in E05-D07.

## Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
  Given a token change dropping color.text.secondary to 4.2:1 on surface.app

Scenario: Undeclared token fails loudly
  Given a new colour token with no entry in the pair registry

Scenario: Heatmap stops validated individually
  Given a 6-stop heatmap ramp
```

title: Create icon registry and custom trading-domain icons
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/16-design-system-brief.md#5-iconography` requires a single outline icon set at 16/20/24px optical sizes with 1.5px stroke, referenced by semantic `IconName` strings and never by raw inline SVG in component code, plus a set of custom trading-domain icons that no generic library provides. CMP-019 Icon's completeness test depends on the registry existing.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/ui/src/icons/` registry: a typed `IconName` union, one component per icon, at a bounded registry cost, all drawn on the 1.5px-stroke grid at the three optical sizes (`size.icon.sm/md/lg`).
- Base set sourced from an open library (Lucide/Phosphor-equivalent), imported as a curated subset rather than the whole library.
- Custom trading-domain icons authored to the same grid: flatten-all, chase-limit, iceberg-order, TWAP, one-click-arm, native-SL-shield, estimated/heuristic badge glyph, node-graph node-type glyphs (trigger, condition, action, logic-gate, comment), heatmap-convention swap.
- Each icon registered with a canonical name and a short semantic description (feeds CMP-019's completeness test and the Figma icon page).
- Lint rule: raw `<svg>` in component source outside `src/icons/` fails; icon-only controls must supply `aria-label`; icon adjacent to visible text must be `aria-hidden`.

## Out of scope
- Brand/logo artwork.
- Icons for features not yet designed (add them with their owning epic).
- Animated icons.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Registry completeness
  Given the IconName union
  When the completeness test runs
  Then every name maps to an exported component and every component is reachable by exactly one name
Scenario: Custom icons match the grid
  Given any custom trading icon
  Then its stroke width is 1.5px and its bounding box matches the base set at each optical size
Scenario: Decorative vs meaningful is enforced
  Given an icon-only IconButton without an aria-label
  When lint and the axe story check run
  Then both fail
Scenario: No inline SVG leakage
  Given a component embedding a raw svg element
  When lint runs
  Then it fails naming the file and pointing at the registry
Scenario: Bounded registry cost
  Given an app rendering icons through the by-name Icon
  When the bundle is analysed
  Then the whole icon registry adds at most 15 KB gzipped
```

## Technical notes / design
Icons compile from SVG source to React components at build time (SVGR or equivalent) with `currentColor` fills so they inherit the semantic colour token from their context - never hardcoded fills. `size.icon.sm/md/lg` map to 16/20/24px. Descriptions live alongside the name in a single `registry.ts` so the Figma icon page and the code stay comparable by diff.

## Test plan
Unit: completeness test (every name renders; every export is named); snapshot of the rendered SVG per icon at each size; a `currentColor` assertion so no icon hardcodes a fill. Lint-rule tests for the raw-SVG and aria-label rules. Bundle test asserting the registry's gzipped cost. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
Third-party SVG source is executable-adjacent content: icons are compiled from vetted SVG files committed to the repo, never fetched at runtime; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Included in E05-X02's dependency review.

## Accessibility notes
The decorative-vs-meaningful rule is binding, not stylistic (`16-design-system-brief.md#5`): icon+text is `aria-hidden`; icon-only carries `aria-label`. The estimated/heuristic glyph is an accessibility-critical icon because it is the non-colour cue that a value is inferred rather than exchange-provided.

## Performance notes
Icons must not ship as a single monolithic sprite import: each glyph is its own module. The registry adds <=15 KB gzipped. The by-name `Icon` imports every glyph, so the bound is on the whole registry, not on per-screen tree-shaking (AC amended 2026-10-27, orchestrator ruling on #4799).

## Context
The three-tier token model, the Style Dictionary multi-target build, the decision to express density as alias resolution rather than a parallel scale, and the decision to deliver theme colours to the WebGL engine as a separate uniforms JSON are architectural decisions with long-lived consequences for E11 (engine core) and E10 (Electron shell). `docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md` requires such decisions to be recorded; without an ADR, the next engineer re-litigates them (risk R10).

## Scope / Deliverables

Shipping these first unblocks S02/S03 and the R1 screen epics. This is the first engineering story of E05 and therefore the one that establishes the pattern every later component follows.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/ui/src/components/`: CMP-001 Button, CMP-002 IconButton, CMP-003 SegmentedControl, CMP-004 Toggle (Switch), CMP-005 Checkbox, CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-007 TextInput, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-009 Select, CMP-010 Slider.

- Server-backed state of any kind.

```gherkin
Scenario: Full matrix is rendered and snapshot-stable

  When its Storybook stories are built
  Then every Variant x State combination documented in 15-component-catalogue.md has a story
  And each renders in dark, light and high-contrast at both densities
Scenario: Keyboard contract
  Given CMP-003 SegmentedControl has focus
  When ArrowRight is pressed
  Then selection moves to the next option per the WAI-ARIA radiogroup pattern and is announced

  When it is clicked or activated with Enter twice
  Then onClick fires zero additional times and the control is announced as busy
Scenario: No hardcoded values
  When lint runs over these components
  Then zero raw hex or px values are reported
```

Each component follows the WAI-ARIA APG pattern named in its catalogue entry: Button (button), SegmentedControl (radiogroup), Toggle (switch), Checkbox (checkbox with indeterminate), RadioGroup (radiogroup with roving tabindex), TextInput/NumericStepperInput (textbox with `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`), Select (the native-pattern dropdown documented in the catalogue - native `select` semantics, styled shell), Slider (slider with `aria-valuemin/max/now/text`). Props are typed with no `any`; `mypy`-equivalent strictness is TypeScript `strict` from E02. PageUp/PageDown/Home/End. a11y: `vitest-axe` per story, zero serious/critical. Visual regression: baseline captured by E05-T04 across theme x density. Fixtures: none external. Atoms must render without layout-measuring effects (no ResizeObserver, no `getBoundingClientRect` in render) so a 500-row table of inputs stays inside the frame budget in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. ## Context
The second atom band carries the system's information-display and feedback vocabulary: typography primitives (the mechanism that enforces tabular numerics app-wide), status badges, loading and empty/error states, tooltips/popovers, and the small utilities that later trading components depend on (CMP-032 confidence dots and CMP-034 MaskedValue in particular are safety-relevant). `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` section 1 specifies each entry.

- CMP-020 NumericText enforces `font.feature.tabularNums` at the component level (catalogue rule: 'enforced at the CMP-020 level, not left to per-usage CSS').
- CMP-031 ColorSwatch and CMP-037 SwatchLegendItem are the primitives SCR-116 uses for palette selection (US-SET-005).
- CMP-032 Confidence Dots is the non-colour cue for estimated/heuristic values.
- Full Storybook matrix, interaction stories where interactive (Tooltip, Popover, CopyButton, MaskedValue), unit tests.

## Out of scope
- CMP-227 EstimatedBadge (trading band, later epic) - CMP-032 is its dependency only.
- Molecules (E05-S03).
- CMP-024 Sparkline data-fetching or streaming behaviour; it takes a static array in v0.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tabular numerics are enforced centrally
  Given a column of values rendered with CMP-020 NumericText
  Then every glyph advances identically and the digits align, with tabular-nums applied by the component and not by the consumer
Scenario: Tooltip keyboard and dismissal
  Given a focusable trigger with a Tooltip
  When it receives keyboard focus
  Then the tooltip appears and is linked via aria-describedby
  And Escape dismisses it while focus remains on the trigger
Scenario: Popover focus management
  Given an open Popover
  Then focus is moved into it, Tab is contained where the catalogue specifies a trap, and Escape returns focus to the trigger
Scenario: Masked value never leaks by default
  Given CMP-034 MaskedValue holding a secret
  Then the default state is masked, reveal is explicit, and the revealed value auto-remasks after the configured timeout
Scenario: Estimated confidence is not colour-only
  Given CMP-032 rendering low confidence
  Then the level is conveyed by filled-dot count and an accessible text label, not by hue alone
Scenario: Skeleton respects reduced motion
  Given data-motion="reduce"
  When a Skeleton renders
  Then the shimmer loop does not run and a static two-tone fill is shown
Scenario: Empty and error states are first-class
  Given CMP-026 and CMP-027
  Then each renders a title, a description and an optional action, and is announced appropriately (error via role="alert" where transient)
```

## Technical notes / design
Tooltip/Popover built on a single positioning primitive shared between them so behaviour cannot diverge; collision handling flips rather than clips. CMP-024 Sparkline renders to inline SVG (not canvas) at this size so it stays accessible and snapshot-testable; it exposes an accessible summary (`role="img"` plus a computed label such as '12 points, trending up 3.4%'). CMP-034 MaskedValue: reveal is a deliberate action, never a hover; copy-to-clipboard copies without logging and announces 'copied' politely. CMP-039 FocusRing is a non-visual utility export (a CSS class/mixin plus a hook) consumed by every interactive component rather than each redefining `:focus-visible`.

## Test plan
Unit per component (props/variants/states). Interaction: Tooltip focus/Escape, Popover focus containment and restore, CopyButton clipboard mock, MaskedValue reveal/auto-remask timer with fake timers. a11y: `vitest-axe` per story; explicit assertions for `aria-describedby` wiring, `role="alert"`, and Sparkline's accessible name. Reduced-motion tests for Spinner/Skeleton. Visual regression via E05-T04. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
CMP-034 MaskedValue is directly security-relevant: it will display API-key fragments and TOTP recovery codes in E09/E27. Requirements: masked by default, explicit reveal, time-limited reveal, no value in DOM attributes when masked, never written to logs or analytics, clipboard write does not echo the value. This component must be re-reviewed by the Security engineer in E05-X02. Data classification of the component's *inputs*: secret.

## Accessibility notes
Tooltip and Popover are the two most commonly mis-implemented a11y patterns - both must follow the APG pattern exactly, including Escape handling and focus restore. All status-carrying atoms (Badge, Tag, Callout, Confidence Dots) pair colour with icon/text per `05-accessibility-standard.md` section 4. Live-region usage is deliberately conservative to avoid the verbosity problem US-SET-007 calls out.

## Performance notes
Sparkline must handle up to 200 points without measurable jank; Skeleton shimmer is CSS-only. No atom may attach a global scroll or resize listener - positioning primitives attach listeners only while an overlay is open.

## Observability
CopyButton and MaskedValue expose optional callbacks so consuming screens (e.g. key management) can emit audit events; the atoms themselves emit nothing.

title: Implement molecules: forms, overlays, table and navigation primitives
body:
## Context
Molecules compose the atoms into the patterns every screen reuses: form fields with labels and errors, menus, tabs, dialogs (including the confirm-dialog pattern that US-SET-003's destructive-action policy will build on), toasts, drawers, the base data table that every grid in the app derives from, and the command palette that US-SET-002's global hotkey layer opens (SCR-012). `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` section 2 specifies each.

## Scope / Deliverables
- CMP-040 FormField, CMP-041 Menu, CMP-042 Tabs, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-045 Toast, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-047 DatePicker/DateRangePicker, CMP-048 Combobox/AutoComplete, CMP-049 Table (base data table), CMP-050 Card, CMP-054 SearchBox, CMP-059 CommandPalette, CMP-065 FormSection, CMP-069 InfoPanel.
- CMP-044 ConfirmDialog ships all three confirm gates as variants - standard dialog, typed-confirm, and hold-to-confirm with a visible progress indicator and configurable 300-2000 ms duration - because US-SET-003 (Must) requires the policy and the hold duration to be configurable, and the later settings screen must not invent its own control.
- CMP-049 Table ships the zoom/text-scale reflow behaviour required by `16-design-system-brief.md#3` rule 4 (at high zoom, dense tables reflow to a stacked/card layout rather than clipping) as a required, tested state.
- CMP-059 CommandPalette provides the primitive SCR-012 composes; the global hotkey registration itself is E10.
- Full Storybook matrix, interaction stories, unit tests.

## Out of scope
- CMP-051..CMP-053, CMP-055..CMP-058, CMP-060, CMP-061, CMP-064, CMP-066..CMP-068 (deferred to the epic that first needs them).
- Screens composing these (SCR-012, SCR-029 etc.) - later epics.
- Virtualised rendering for very large tables (added by the epic that first needs 10k+ rows); v0 Table renders a bounded row count.
- Server-side sorting/pagination.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Form field wires label, help and error
  Given CMP-040 with a label, help text and an error
  Then the control has an accessible name from the label, aria-describedby referencing both help and error, and aria-invalid true
  And the label is persistent, never placeholder-only
Scenario: Dialog focus contract
  Given an open CMP-043 Dialog
  Then focus moves to the dialog, Tab is trapped inside, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the invoking element
  And the background is inert to both pointer and screen reader
Scenario: Hold-to-confirm gate
  Given CMP-044 in hold variant with an 800 ms duration
  When the user presses and releases after 400 ms
  Then the action does not fire and the progress indicator resets
  And a keyboard-only path exists that achieves the same gate without a pointer
Scenario: Typed confirm
  Given CMP-044 in typed variant requiring the text FLATTEN
  When any other text is entered
  Then the confirm control remains disabled with a stated reason
Scenario: Table reflow at 200% zoom
  Given a dense CMP-049 Table in compact density
  When the page is zoomed to 200%
  Then rows reflow to a stacked layout with no horizontal clipping and no loss of any column's data
Scenario: Toast does not steal focus
  Given a Toast appears while the user is typing
  Then focus is not moved, and the message is announced politely (assertively only for errors)
Scenario: Combobox keyboard
  Given CMP-048 with filtered options
  When ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Enter/Escape are used
  Then the APG combobox pattern is followed and the active option is announced
```

## Technical notes / design
Overlays (Dialog, Drawer, Popover-based Menu, CommandPalette) share one focus-management primitive and one scroll-lock primitive so behaviour cannot diverge per component; inertness uses `inert` where supported with an `aria-hidden` fallback. Toast host is a single portal (the CMP-212 ToastHost organism later wraps it). CMP-049 Table exposes column definitions declaratively, supports sticky header, keyboard row navigation and per-cell `NumericText` usage for numeric columns (mono/tabular/right-aligned per cross-cutting rule 6). Reflow threshold is expressed in `em` so it tracks text scale rather than device pixels.

## Test plan
Unit per component. Interaction: dialog focus trap and restore, Escape handling, hold-to-confirm timing with fake timers (fires at >=duration, not before), typed-confirm disabled-until-match, combobox keyboard matrix, tabs roving tabindex, table keyboard navigation and reflow at simulated 200% zoom. a11y: `vitest-axe` per story plus explicit assertions for dialog `aria-modal`, toast live-region politeness, and form-field description wiring. Visual regression via E05-T04 incl. the reflowed table state. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
CMP-044 ConfirmDialog is a safety control: it will gate flatten, cancel-all, reverse and freeze (US-SET-003). Threats: a confirm gate that can be satisfied programmatically or by a stray Enter keypress defeats the safety invariant. Tests must prove the hold gate cannot be satisfied by a single synthetic click and that the typed gate requires exact text. Flagged for the Security engineer's review in E05-X02. No secrets handled directly.

## Accessibility notes
Dialog/Drawer/Menu/Combobox each follow their APG pattern exactly. The hold-to-confirm gate must have a documented, tested keyboard-only equivalent - a pointer-only safety gate would exclude keyboard users from destructive actions entirely, which `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 3.1 forbids. Table reflow at 200% zoom implements section 5.7 of that standard. Toast politeness levels follow section 6.2.

## Performance notes
Table must render its bounded v0 row count within one frame; overlay open/close uses the motion recipes (CSS transitions) so no JS animation loop runs. Scroll-lock must not cause layout shift (compensate for scrollbar width).

## Observability
ConfirmDialog exposes an `onConfirm` metadata callback carrying the gate variant used, so downstream trading screens can write the audit event that `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-SET-003 requires ('the choice is audited').

- [ ] Coverage gate green.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` updated where implementation diverged.
- [ ] axe-core green; manual screen-reader pass on Dialog, Combobox and Table.

## Context
US-SET-004 (themes and density, Must), US-SET-005 (colour conventions and CVD-safe palettes, Must) and US-SET-007 (accessibility preferences, Must) are delivered on SCR-116 and SCR-117 by the later settings epic - but those screens are explicitly composed (per `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` rows US-SET-004/005/007) from CMP-062 ThemeSwitcher, CMP-063 DensityToggle, CMP-031 ColorSwatch, CMP-037 SwatchLegendItem, CMP-228 PreviewTile, CMP-065 FormSection and CMP-069 InfoPanel. This story ships the design-system half so the settings epic assembles rather than invents. It also ships the app-state components (CMP-079, CMP-085, CMP-089, CMP-090, CMP-091) the E10 shell needs on day one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- CMP-062 ThemeSwitcher: dark / light / high-contrast selection driving the E05-T02 runtime, plus the optional 'match system' mode (default off).
- CMP-063 DensityToggle: compact / comfortable, global and per-panel scoped.
- CMP-228 PreviewTile: renders a live sample of a chart cell, a ladder row and a positions row under the currently-selected theme/density/palette - the control SCR-116 uses to preview a choice before committing it.
- CMP-079 RbacGate: the disabled-with-reason wrapper; in v0 it takes an explicit `allowed`/`reason` pair (the RBAC policy source arrives with E09).
- CMP-085 SkipLink, CMP-089 ForbiddenState (403), CMP-090 NotFoundState (404), CMP-091 GlobalErrorBoundaryFallback.
- Storybook stories demonstrating all three themes x two densities x motion-safe/reduce.
- US ids served: US-SET-004, US-SET-005, US-SET-007 (system-level primitives), plus the shell's 403/404/error surfaces.

## Out of scope
- SCR-116 and SCR-117 screens themselves, and persistence of preferences to the server (settings epic).
- The actual RBAC policy decision point and role model (E09).
- Chart palette *application* to WebGL surfaces (E11) - PreviewTile renders a static representative sample, not a live engine canvas.
- Crash reporting wiring behind CMP-091 (E10).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Theme switch is immediate and complete
  Given CMP-062 in any story
  When high-contrast is selected
  Then the root data-theme becomes high-contrast within one frame, buy/sell resolve to their .hc variants, and no component remounts
Scenario: Match-system is opt-in
  Given a fresh profile
  Then 'match system' is off and the explicit user choice governs
Scenario: Preview before commit
  Given CMP-228 PreviewTile and a candidate CVD-safe palette
  When the palette is selected in the preview
  Then the tile updates to show a chart cell, a ladder row and a positions row in that palette without applying it globally
Scenario: Contrast warning on a failing combination
  Given a candidate custom palette whose text pair falls below 4.5:1
  When it is previewed
  Then a warning is shown stating the combination fails contrast
Scenario: Disabled-with-reason
  Given CMP-079 wrapping an action with allowed=false and reason "Viewer role cannot place orders"
  Then the control is non-operable, the reason is visible on hover and focus and present in the accessible description
Scenario: Skip link
  Given a page with CMP-085 as the first focusable element
  When Tab is pressed from the document start
  Then the skip link becomes visible and activating it moves focus to the main landmark
Scenario: Error boundary fallback
  Given a child component throws
  Then CMP-091 renders with a description, a retry action and a reference id, and the error does not blank the whole shell
```

## Technical notes / design
CMP-062/CMP-063 subscribe to the E05-T02 external store for their own checked state only - they must not cause a tree-wide re-render (this is the component-level half of the no-remount guarantee). CMP-228 PreviewTile renders DOM/SVG samples using the same semantic tokens the engine will later consume, and takes an optional token-override map so a candidate palette can be previewed without mutating the document root. The contrast warning reuses the ratio function shipped by E05-T05 rather than a second implementation. CMP-079 exposes `allowed`, `reason` and an optional `requiredRole` for message templating; it renders the reason via tooltip plus `aria-describedby`, never as a bare disabled attribute.

## Test plan
Unit: theme/density setters, match-system default off, RbacGate blocks handler invocation, error boundary catches and renders fallback, 403/404 states render their documented content. Interaction: keyboard operation of ThemeSwitcher and DensityToggle; skip-link tab-then-activate path; preview palette override does not leak to the document root. a11y: axe per story; explicit assertion that the reason text is in the accessible description. Perf: reuse E05-T02's no-remount assertion in a story containing a 500-row table plus these controls. Visual regression across the full theme x density matrix. Coverage >=80%.

## Security notes
CMP-079 RbacGate is a **UI affordance, not an authorisation control** - this must be stated in its docs and its Storybook notes: server-side deny-by-default enforcement (E09) is the real control, and a disabled button is never the security boundary. This note is a required outcome of E05-X01's STRIDE model (spoofing/elevation branch) and is re-checked in E05-X02. CMP-089 ForbiddenState must not leak why access was denied beyond the role requirement (no resource existence disclosure).

## Accessibility notes
This story is the a11y showcase band: SCR-117 is described in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` as 'itself the exemplar'. The high-contrast theme, the reduce-motion pathway and the skip link all land here. Every control has a visible persistent label and its state announced on change. PreviewTile must expose its sample content as text as well as visuals so a screen-reader user can evaluate a palette choice's labelling, not just its colours.

## Performance notes
Theme/density switch inherits E05-T02's one-frame budget; PreviewTile must re-render on palette change in <=16.6 ms. No GL context is created by PreviewTile in v0 (explicitly a DOM/SVG sample) precisely to avoid context-loss risk during rapid palette browsing.

CMP-062/CMP-063 invoke the injectable analytics callback with `appearance.theme_changed` and `appearance.density_changed`; the a11y preference controls emit `a11y.preference_changed` `{key, value}`. The package ships a no-op default so `packages/ui` stays app-agnostic.

title: STRIDE threat model: design-system supply chain and Storybook exposure
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` require a STRIDE threat model per epic. E05 handles no money and no secrets at runtime, which is exactly why it is easy to skip - and exactly why it is an attractive target: the design system is a build-time dependency of every frontend surface, so a compromised token build or icon pipeline executes in every developer's machine and in CI, and a leaked Storybook exposes the entire unreleased product surface.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE analysis over the E05 trust boundaries: (1) design tool -> repo (Tokens Studio export, any Figma automation token), (2) third-party build dependencies (Style Dictionary, Storybook and addons, icon library, SVG compiler, VR tool), (3) CI -> artefact publication (Storybook static build, VR baselines), (4) library -> consuming app (the CSP inline-script hash from E05-T02; the RbacGate-is-not-authorisation boundary).
- Abuse cases: malicious dependency executing at token-build time with repo credentials; typosquatted icon package; Storybook published to an internet-reachable host; VR screenshots of unreleased trading UI leaving the network via a SaaS; a component prop rendered as HTML enabling stored XSS in a later screen; an attacker relying on a disabled button as the only control.
- Mitigations mapped to concrete tickets/controls (lockfile pinning, least-privileged CI token, gitleaks path rule over `tokens/`, Tailscale-only hosting, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` lint rule, CSP hash rather than `unsafe-inline`, explicit docs that RbacGate is an affordance).
- Residual-risk statement with the Owner's acceptance where applicable (e.g. SaaS VR tool).
- Findings recorded in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md` where they represent new project risks.

## Out of scope

- Exchange-boundary and OMS threat models (E08/E29).
- Pen-test (R4, E43).

```gherkin

  Given the four named trust boundaries
  When the model is reviewed
  Then each boundary has an explicit entry for spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service and elevation, or a stated 'not applicable' with a reason

Scenario: Supply-chain control is concrete

Scenario: Storybook exposure is closed

```

## Test plan

Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.

title: Security review of design-system dependencies, CSP impact and Storybook hosting
body:
## Context
E05-X01 models the threats; this ticket verifies that what actually shipped implements the mitigations. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 8 requires a Security-engineer review comment before Done for anything the model flags, and R0's quality gate requires zero unresolved Critical/High from SAST/SCA/secrets scanning.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Dependency review of the shipped `packages/ui` tree: `npm audit`/SCA results triaged; Storybook, Style Dictionary, icon and VR tooling dependencies checked for known CVEs, unmaintained packages and postinstall scripts.
- Verify the CSP consequence of E05-T02's pre-paint inline script: confirm it is allowlisted by hash, not by `unsafe-inline`, and hand the exact hash-generation requirement to E10 in writing.
- Verify Storybook hosting is not internet-reachable and that the published build contains no realistic account/key/PnL fixture data.
- Verify the gitleaks path rule over `packages/ui/tokens/**` is active and that no secret is present in token files.
- Component-level checks: CMP-034 MaskedValue (masked by default, time-limited reveal, no logging, clipboard does not echo, screen reader does not announce the secret), CMP-044 ConfirmDialog gates (cannot be satisfied by a single synthetic event), CMP-079 RbacGate (documented as an affordance, not an authorisation control), and a repo-wide check that no component uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- Triage findings: fix, or record accepted risk with a dated Owner sign-off.

## Out of scope
- Auth/RBAC implementation review (E09).
- DAST/ZAP runs against the application (no app surface in E05).
- Pen-test (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Zero unresolved Critical or High
  Given the SCA and secrets scans over packages/ui
  When the review concludes
  Then no Critical or High finding remains unresolved, and each Medium has a dated accepted-risk entry
Scenario: CSP is not weakened
  Given the pre-paint inline script
  Then it is allowlisted by hash and the requirement is recorded on the E10 ticket; an unsafe-inline allowance fails the review
Scenario: Secret handling verified
  Given CMP-034 MaskedValue with a secret value
  When it is inspected in the DOM, the console, analytics and under a screen reader while masked
  Then the value appears in none of them
Scenario: Safety gate cannot be bypassed
  Given CMP-044 in hold variant
  When a single synthetic click event is dispatched
  Then the action does not fire
Scenario: No HTML injection surface
  When the package is scanned for dangerouslySetInnerHTML
  Then zero occurrences exist
```

## Technical notes / design
Run the same scanners the pipeline uses (npm audit / the project's SCA tool, gitleaks, CodeQL for the JS/TS surface) so results are directly comparable to CI. For the postinstall-script check, enumerate packages with install hooks and justify each retained one.

## Test plan
Every check above is automated where possible so the review is repeatable: the `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` scan becomes a lint rule, the MaskedValue checks become unit/interaction tests, the ConfirmDialog synthetic-event check becomes an interaction test (shared with E05-Q03's pack).

## Security notes
This ticket is the security gate for the epic. Data classification: the package handles no secrets itself but CMP-034 renders them; treat its contract as secret-adjacent. Security label mandatory; no Done without the reviewer's comment.

## Accessibility notes
Cross-check: the MaskedValue screen-reader behaviour is both an a11y and a security property - it must announce that a value is hidden without announcing the value.

## Performance notes
N/A.

## Observability
Scan results attached to the ticket and available as CI artefacts; accepted risks recorded with dates and owners so they resurface at the R4 pen-test.

- [ ] SCA/secrets/SAST results triaged; zero unresolved Critical/High.
- [ ] CSP hash requirement written onto the E10 ticket.
- [ ] Storybook hosting confirmed private; fixtures confirmed synthetic.
- [ ] Component-level checks automated and green.
